summary: Striped resort tower on Hilton Head Island, built 1969-70 for Sea Pines by Charles Fraser; owned by the resort and climbable for a fee.

structures.note: 90 ft (27.4 m) per the owner, the island visitor website and Clio; completed spring 1970. Octagonal per LighthouseFriends; hexagonal per the owner.

access.note: Climbable for a small fee; museum panels on the landings; owned by the resort. LighthouseFriends gives the hours as daily from 10 a.m. to sunset; Clio's listing gives 10 AM to 7:30 PM.

notes_for_editor: 1) No keepers, wrecks or rescues are sourced to this tower; the keepers and storms chapters are omitted. 2) The station record's Coast Guard number 3-4375 is, in the 2011 Light List copy read (Volume III, entries 4375-4390), 'Harbour Town - LIGHT 1', a private green light on a pile (Fl G 6s). LIGHT 2 (4380, QR), LIGHT 3 (4385, QG) and LIGHT 4 (4390, QR) are also private aids. The tower is not listed under its own name in that edition, so the record's 3-4375 probably belongs to a marina light, not the tower. Check against the current Light List (2024/2025 PDFs returned HTTP 403). 3) Characteristic: LighthouseFriends gives a white flash with a 30-second period and 15-mile visibility, the only characteristic in the story. The record's 'Q R' comes from ENC and is not in any source cited here; Wikipedia's infobox (Fl W 2.5s) is a lead only and is not cited. The story does not state a disagreement, because no cited source gives a conflicting figure; the record's figure needs a check. 4) Height: 90 ft (27.4 m) per the owner, visitor site and Clio; Wikipedia gives 93 ft (28 m) citing Hilton Head Monthly 2014, which returned HTTP 500 and was not read; the record says 27.0 m. 5) Steps: 104 (owner) vs 114 (visitor site, Clio). 6) Shape: octagonal (LighthouseFriends) vs hexagonal (owner's site, which also gives stucco over a steel frame). 7) The visitor website's claim that Fraser moved a pair of keepers' houses from an 1863 island lighthouse to Harbour Town in 1969 is unverified and not used. 8) The owner's and visitor websites are promotional; used only for measured facts (height, steps, exterior material, stripe choice). 9) Clio says the lighthouse was built by 'boosters and developers'; not used. 10) Hours disagree: LighthouseFriends (daily 10 a.m. to sunset) against Clio (10 AM to 7:30 PM, a 2020 listing). Check before relying on either for a visit. 11) The first lighting date (1970 in the record) is not given in the primary-type sources read; the story gives completion in spring 1970 instead. 12) Verification 2026-10-28: removed 'the marina sits on Calibogue Sound' (no cited source says it) and the sentence claiming the sources disagree on the light without a conflicting source; changed 'opened in 1956' to 'was built' (LighthouseFriends says constructed) and footnoted it; 'mocked' attributed to the Sun, the doubters' naming to LighthouseFriends; metric equivalents added; the record's 'metal lath over plywood' material removed (no source); access note corrected (hours are given); resolved_conflicts emptied (shape is unresolved, and Clio gives no shape).
